quote_free_scope_diagnosis: The paper assumes a maximally complete base field with full positive-real value group. Extending an arbitrary original field into that domain would still require actual metric recognition, invariance and descent, not just the existence of a field extension.

Its semipositive class is introduced using pointwise limits of FS metrics. Its norm envelopes are potentially discontinuous or degenerate. Identification with the user-task ACTUAL decreasing-FS-net PSH/E1 class is an additional unproved application premise.

Theorem3.28 compares the equidistribution measure with genuine MA only for a CONTINUOUS semipositive Shilov-finite metric. Proposition4.8 prescribes a finite equidistribution measure, with additional lower-norm bounds yielding a non-degenerate metric; it still allows singular metrics. Remark4.9 explicitly retains continuity/regularization for genuine MA comparison.

The inverse construction uses norms formed from finitely many birational cone points and nonnegative simplex coordinates. The continuity argument uses finite matrices of logarithmic evaluations and a mapping-degree argument on simplex faces. Zero coordinates need an independent finite-matrix/limit justification: positive-degree evaluations there can be zero, distinct scaled points can coincide at the cone vertex, and logarithms are not ordinary finite real entries. No such repair is granted here.

The Proposition3.13/Theorem3.17 printed error estimates are of order n^d, while chi(n) for dimX=d has order n^d. These displayed orders alone do not establish a vanishing normalized error or the subsequent1/n estimate. A sharper order, an additional normalization, or an independently reconstructed reduction/conductor argument must be verified. This is a proof-audit concern, not a concluded counterexample to the main theorem.

The reduction-Proj/tautological ampleness/component Hilbert-polynomial/conductor arguments in Proposition3.13 require exact justification for the permitted general non-affinoid Shilov-finite norm. No finite-generation/Noetherian reduction premise is silently inserted.

Thus this source currently supplies a possible analytic route, not an accepted arbitrary-target actual finite-energy equation. No full original or partial proof acceptance follows from the abstract or printed surjectivity claim.
